title: Avoid embedding full Rock pages as public concierge app surfaces
distilled_summary: When building a public Rock-backed concierge or Helix UI, avoid treating a full Rock page iframe as the long-term integration contract. Full-page iframe embedding can be blocked by Content Security Policy frame-ancestors rules, and sandboxed iframes can also change origin behavior in ways that break HTMX or authenticated page assumptions. Prefer a page-hosted Lava Application Content block, a purpose-built Helix endpoint, or a small read-only adapter that returns only approved public fields to the trusted renderer. If an existing Rock application must remain available, route users to it as a top-level page and keep any person-backed form state, POST endpoints, SMS verification, workflow activation, and mutation paths behind a separate explicit test or launch protocol.
